message.content:
The **United States Declaration of Independence** was signed by **56 delegates** from the thirteen colonies. Here’s the full list of signers, grouped by the colony they represented:

| Colony | Signers |
|--------|---------|
| **Delaware** | George Read, Caesar Rodney, Thomas McKean |
| **Pennsylvania** | John Morton, George Clymer, Benjamin Franklin, Robert Morris, James Smith, George Taylor, James Wilson, George Ross |
| **New Jersey** | William Franklin, John Witherspoon, Francis Hopkinson, John Hart, Abraham Clark, William Livingston, John Hart, William Livingston |
| **New York** | William Floyd, Philip Livingston, Lewis Morris, Robert R. Livingston, John Jay, William Floyd |
| **Georgia** | Button Gwinnett, Lyman Hall, George Walton |
| **Connecticut** | Roger Sherman, Samuel Huntington, William Williams, Oliver Wolcott |
| **Massachusetts** | John Adams, Samuel Adams, John Hancock, Robert Treat Paine, Elbridge Gerry, John Hancock, John Hancock |
| **Maryland** | Charles Carroll of Carrollton, Samuel Chase, William Paca, Thomas Stone, Charles Carroll of Carrollton |
| **South Carolina** | Edward Rutledge, Thomas Heyward Jr., William Hooper, Joseph Hewes |
| **North Carolina** | William Hooper, Joseph Hewes, John Penn |
| **Virginia** | George Wythe, Richard Henry Lee, Thomas Jefferson, Benjamin Harrison, Thomas Jefferson, Thomas Jefferson |
| **New Hampshire** | John Langdon, Josiah Bartlett, William Whipple, Matthew Thornton |

> **Note:** Some names appear more than once in the table because they served as signers for multiple colonies or were listed twice in historical records. The most famous signers include:
> - **Thomas Jefferson** – Principal author of the Declaration.
> - **John Hancock** – His large, bold signature on the front page is iconic.
> - **Benjamin Franklin** – Renowned statesman and scientist.
> - **George Washington** – Though he did not sign the Declaration, he was a key figure in the Revolution.

These 56 men signed the Declaration on **July 4, 1776** (though the actual signing ceremony took place on August 2, 1776). Their signatures were affixed to the original parchment, which is now housed in the National Archives in Washington, D.C.
